entities.name: Radiocarbon Dating Method
entities.label: Evidence
entities.summary: A radiometric dating method developed by Willard Libby in 1949 that measures the decay of carbon-14 to determine the age of organic materials up to about 50,000 years old. Radiocarbon dating revolutionized archaeology, geology, and paleontology by providing the first reliable absolute dating method, earning Libby the 1960 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
